summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 40 (desktop vault settings integration) using the GSD workflow, then refactor duplicated versioning logic discovered during execution.
summary.outcome: Phase 40 planned and executed successfully (2 plans, 2 waves, 9/9 verification must-haves passed), then versioning logic extracted from duplicated platform-specific code into a shared `apply_versioning()` helper function.

repo: macOS and Linux FUSE code paths share the same `fuser`-based `mount_filesystem()` in `crates/fuse/src/fuse/mod.rs` — Linux is not a separate target for the desktop app but shares the macOS code path via the `fuse` feature gate.

Windows FUSE uses WinFSP's `cleanup()` callback in `platform/windows/write_ops.rs` while macOS/Linux use `fuser`'s `release()` callback in `read_ops.rs` — this is why versioning logic was duplicated across platforms.
Phase 40 had no formal REQ-IDs; it was a follow-up to Phase 39 with goal-level coverage only.
The vault settings HKDF derivation uses `cipherbox-vault-settings-v1` as the info string, following the same pattern as 5 existing derivation functions in the crypto crate.
Vault settings load during desktop login via IPNS resolve + ECIES decrypt with graceful fallback to defaults.

code.finding: Versioning decision + pruning logic (cooldown check, version entry construction, pruning) was duplicated here for macOS/Linux; now replaced with call to `helpers::apply_versioning()`.

Near-identical versioning logic duplicated from read_ops.rs; Windows version had underscore-prefixed variables (`_old_encrypted_key`, `_old_iv`) marking them as 'unused', which were actually used. Now replaced with `helpers::apply_versioning()` and variable names de-prefixed.
`helpers.rs` is the platform-agnostic shared module for the fuse crate — correct place to add `apply_versioning()` shared function. Net reduction of ~84 lines of duplicated code.
`mount_filesystem()` is shared between macOS and Linux via the `fuse` feature gate — Linux platform coverage is implicit through this shared entry point.

workflow: Worktree-isolated subagents produce commits on a detached/different branch; cherry-picking onto the feature branch is needed after the worktree merge when automatic merge fails.
The GSD verifier passed 9/9 must-haves even though Linux coverage was implicit rather than explicit — verification doesn't catch architectural concerns like abstraction leakage.
Incorrect architectural claims made in conversational responses (Linux not shipped) were not reflected in planning artifacts — artifact correctness and conversational accuracy can diverge.

friction: Worktree merge for Wave 2 failed silently — commits were on a detached branch, requiring manual cherry-pick onto the feature branch.
An incorrect claim was made conversationally that Linux desktop isn't shipped, which required investigation and retraction after verification passed.
The `verify key-links` tool could not validate Wave 2 target patterns before Wave 2 ran (files didn't exist yet), producing noise in the pre-wave dependency check.
open_items: Confirm that `apply_versioning()` in helpers.rs has consistent logging across both call sites now that the Windows path previously lacked a log line that the macOS/Linux path had.
The Cargo.lock was modified as part of the versioning refactor commit — worth confirming no unintended dependency changes were included.
